messages:
maria (support): Heads-up — got escalation from AcmeCorp. Canary rollout health tiles in the Console are stuck showing 'in progress' for their last two rollouts (ids 84 and 85). They say the rollout finished ~2h ago but the chart never moved to success/failure breakdown. Ticket #SUP-12345. Can someone triage?

sam (eng-frontend): I can repro in staging. Opened the rollout detail and the top 'health' tiles say 'in progress' but the API /api/rollouts/84/health returns final events. UI chart seems to not be picking up the latest status updates.

monitoring-bot: Alert: canary-status-sync errors increased from 0 to 12 in the last 5m (service: canary-sync-service, namespace: redwood-prod).

maria (support): Customer reported seeing it for hours; they tried refresh/caches. They attached screenshot (link: https://files.redwood/incoming/acme/sup12345-snap.png) and gave repro steps (create canary -> promote -> finish).

sam (eng-frontend): Quick dump of what I see from API in staging:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://console.staging.redwood/api/rollouts/84/health" | jq .
{
  "rollout_id": 84,
  "status": "completed",
  "events": [ ... ],
  "last_event_ts": "2026-03-17T09:12:01Z"
}
```

But the frontend's health tile fetch: GET /internal/ui/rolloutTiles?rollout=84 returns:

```
{ "rollout": 84, "tile_status": "in_progress", "updated_at": 2026-03-17T09:10:02Z }
```

sam (eng-frontend): So backend /health is correct but the tile service that's fed by the canary-status-sync job is stale. Repro steps: 1) finish rollout 2) wait 30s 3) UI shows in_progress.

david (sre): Looking at canary-sync-service logs on prod:

```
2026-03-17T09:05:02Z ERROR canary-sync main.go:142 syncLoop: failed to upsert tile for rollout=84: KeyError: 'status_code'
2026-03-17T09:05:02Z DEBUG canary-sync upstream_response: {"rollout":84,"state":"completed","details":{...}}
```

david (sre): Looks like a schema mismatch — the worker expects `status_code` but upstream changed field name to `state`. Recent deploy?

deploy-bot: Deployed canary-sync-service commit abc123 -> at 2026-03-17T09:04:55Z to production (k8s/redwood/canary-sync-service).

sam (eng-frontend): That deploy matches timing. It probably introduced a change in the small adapter used by the tile pipeline. I can patch the frontend to tolerate both `status_code` and `state`, but probably better to patch the sync service quickly.

maria (support): Customer wants an ETA — they've already paused a release. Any temporary workaround we can ask them to do?

david (sre): Short-term mitigation: restart the canary-sync deployment and flush tile cache, that'll force a fresh reconciliation from /api/rollouts. Commands: `kubectl -n redwood-prod rollout restart deployment/canary-sync-service` and then `redis-cli -h tile-cache del canary:tiles:84` (repeat for affected rollout ids). I'll run restart now, will coordinate with sam for the code fix.

sam (eng-frontend): I'll open a quick patch to the sync adapter to read `state` if `status_code` is missing, and add a regression test. PR #452.

(2 minutes later) david (sre): Restarted canary-sync-service and cleared cache for rollouts 84/85. Logs now:

```
2026-03-17T09:08:34Z INFO canary-sync main.go:syncLoop: reconciled rollout=84 status=completed
2026-03-17T09:08:34Z INFO tile-service updater: pushed tile update for rollout=84
```

sam (eng-frontend): I see the tile-service responded to the push and UI polling returned updated tile_status=completed. Patching the service now and will roll the fix.

maria (support): I messaged AcmeCorp with the workaround (refresh + wait ~1m or ask us to restart their affected rollout tiles). They're asking for confirmation once fixed.

deploy-bot: Deployed canary-sync-service commit fix/restore-status-compat (commit def456) to production at 2026-03-17T09:12:12Z.

sam (eng-frontend): Patch merged and deployed. Added compatibility layer and a unit test checking both `status_code` and `state`. Also added an alert to detect unexpected schema fields.

maria (support): Customer confirms via email: "Tiles now show completed and breakdown. Thanks for the quick help." Closing ticket unless anything else.

david (sre): Adding post-incident note — root cause: schema change in upstream produced KeyError in canary-sync worker, prevented tile updates. Action items: 1) revert-compat PR merged (PR #452), 2) add schema validation + contract tests, 3) add canary-monitoring alert for tile-staleness > 5m.

maria (support): Marking SUP-12345 resolved. Thanks team :thumbsup:
